_meta.source: Private ABE review compilation notes (2025), TRANSES collection
_meta.extraction_method: Manually transcribed by reading rendered page images against the source PDF, page by page, formulas only — not tables/constants (separate future pass).
_meta.status: draft — not yet spot-checked by a second human reviewer; ready for DB import as status=draft, promote to published after review
topic_mapping_notes: Hydrology Transes.pdf → LAND_WATER: Hydrology (reused existing topic name exactly).
Irrigation and Drainage Transes.pdf → LAND_WATER: Irrigation and Drainage Engineering (reused existing topic name exactly).

Open Channel Transes.pdf → MATH_BASIC_ENGG: Fluid Mechanics (reused the topic created in an earlier pass, since open-channel hydraulics is core fluid mechanics). Several formulas here (Froude Number, Orifice discharge V=√2gh) are near-duplicates of entries already in that topic from the earlier Pumps/Fluid Mechanics pass — kept per instructions, since this pass is a separate source document and duplicates across passes/topics are expected.

Power Eng Transes.pdf covers Internal Combustion Engines (pages 1-6), renewable energy overview (Solar/Wind/Hydro, pages 7-8), human/animal/tractor power (pages 7-9), and lubricants (pages 9-11). It was split three ways by actual formula content: mechanical engine formulas → existing POWER_ENERGY_MACHINERY: Internal Combustion Engine; fuel-quality/fuel-energy formulas (octane, cetane, thermal efficiency) → existing POWER_ENERGY_MACHINERY: Fuels and Lubricants; drawbar/rolling-resistance, human-power-output, and draft-animal load formulas → existing POWER_ENERGY_MACHINERY: Agricultural Power and Tractor Operation. The Solar/Wind/Hydro pages contained only definitions and classification tables with no extractable named formulas, so no renewable-energy topic was created for this pass.

Hydrology's SCS Curve Number runoff formula denominator was transcribed as the standard (I + 0.8S) form; the source page render was visually ambiguous (looked like '0.85') and the standard form was used to avoid transcribing a garbled digit as fact.

Hydrology's groundwater-recession equation is transcribed as qt = q0·k^dt per the source's own variable legend, even though the printed equation itself uses 'qo' while the legend labels the same term 'do' — treated as the same symbol (initial/starting discharge).

Irrigation and Drainage's 'flow to left drain' and 'flow to right drain' unsteady-recharge equations were printed with identical expressions in the source; both are retained as separate directional cases exactly as labeled in the original, rather than assuming a sign difference not shown in the source.

entries.title: Drainage Basin Length
entries.variables: L = basin length, A = drainage area
entries.description: Empirical estimate of the distance along the main channel from the watershed outlet to the basin divide.

entries.title: Basin Slope
entries.variables: EL1, EL2 = elevations at the basin divide and outlet, L = basin/flow-path length
entries.description: Rate of change of elevation along the principal flow path of a watershed.

entries.title: Areal Rainfall — Arithmetic Mean Method
entries.variables: Pi = rainfall depth at each station, n = number of stations
entries.description: Simplest estimate of average areal rainfall by averaging all station depths.

entries.title: Areal Rainfall — Thiessen Polygon Method
entries.variables: Ai = area of the Thiessen polygon around station i, pi = rainfall at station i
entries.description: Weights each gage's rainfall by the area it represents, assuming rainfall equals the nearest station's reading.

entries.title: Areal Rainfall — Isohyetal Method
entries.variables: ai = area between successive isohyets, Pi = isohyet value, A = total basin area
entries.description: Weights rainfall by the area enclosed between successive isohyets plotted on a map.

entries.title: Adequacy of Rainfall Stations
entries.variables: N = optimal number of stations, Cv = coefficient of variation, ε = allowable percentage error
entries.description: Determines how many rain gage stations are needed for a target estimation accuracy.

entries.title: Coefficient of Variation (Rainfall Network)
entries.variables: σ(m−1) = standard deviation of station rainfall, P̄ = mean precipitation
entries.description: Relative variability of rainfall across a gage network, used to size the network.

entries.title: Standard Deviation of Station Rainfall
entries.variables: Pi = precipitation at station i, P̄ = mean precipitation, m = number of stations
entries.description: Dispersion of individual station rainfall about the network mean.

entries.title: Mean Precipitation
entries.variables: Pi = precipitation magnitude at the ith station, m = number of stations
entries.description: Average precipitation across a rain gage network.

entries.title: Estimating Missing Rainfall — Arithmetic Mean Method
entries.variables: Px = estimated missing rainfall, Pi = rainfall at m index stations
entries.description: Valid when each index station's normal rainfall is within 10% of the normal rainfall at the missing station.

entries.title: Estimating Missing Rainfall — Normal Ratio Method
entries.variables: Nx, Ni = normal annual rainfall at the missing and index stations, Pi = rainfall at index stations, m = number of index stations
entries.description: Used when an index station's normal rainfall differs from the missing station's by more than 10%.

entries.title: Double Mass Analysis (Rain Gage Consistency)
entries.formula: k = (gradient of line before change) / (gradient of line after change)
entries.variables: Gradients read from the cumulative double-mass curve
entries.description: Correction factor used to check and adjust a rain gage record for inconsistency caused by a change at the station.

entries.title: Recurrence Interval Probability
entries.variables: T = return period (years)
entries.description: Probability that an event of given magnitude will be equaled/exceeded, or not, in any one year.

entries.title: Non-Exceedance Probability Over N Years
entries.variables: T = return period, N = number of years in the series
entries.description: Probability that a design event will NOT occur in any series of N years.

entries.title: Exceedance Probability Over N Years
entries.variables: T = return period, N = number of years in the series
entries.description: Probability that a design event will occur at least once in any series of N years.

entries.title: Probability of an Event Occurring Exactly 2 Times in N Years
entries.variables: n = number of years, p = annual exceedance probability, q = 1−p
entries.description: Binomial probability that a design event occurs exactly twice in n successive years.

entries.title: Weibull Equation (Plotting Position)
entries.variables: T = return period (yrs), n = number of records, m = rank of the event
entries.description: Assigns a return period to a ranked hydrologic record for frequency analysis.

entries.title: Gumbel Distribution (Extreme Value)
entries.variables: XT = magnitude of the event for return period T, M = mean, S = standard deviation of the series
entries.description: Estimates the magnitude of an extreme hydrologic event (e.g. flood) for a given return period.

entries.title: Pan Evaporation Method
entries.variables: kp = pan coefficient, Epan = measured pan evaporation
entries.description: Estimates reference crop evapotranspiration from a Class A pan reading.

entries.title: Evaporation Rate (Vapor Pressure Deficit)
entries.variables: C = empirical constant, ew = saturation vapor pressure at water-surface temperature, ea = vapor pressure of the air
entries.description: Rate of evaporation from a water surface as a function of the vapor pressure deficit.

entries.title: Water-Budget Method (Reservoir Evaporation)
entries.formula: P + Vis + Vig = Vos + Vog + EL + ΔS + TL
entries.variables: P = precipitation, Vis/Vig = surface/groundwater inflow, Vos/Vog = surface/groundwater outflow, EL = evaporation loss, ΔS = storage change, TL = transpiration loss
entries.description: Mass balance used to back-calculate evaporation loss from a reservoir.

entries.title: Penman Equation
entries.variables: Δ = slope of the saturation vapor pressure curve, Rn = net radiation, G = soil/ground heat flux, γ = psychrometric constant, es−ea = vapor pressure deficit, ra, rs = aerodynamic and surface resistance
entries.description: Combined energy-balance and mass-transfer method for computing evaporation from open water surfaces.

entries.title: Penman-Monteith Equation
entries.variables: Δ = slope of vapor pressure curve, Rn = net radiation, G = soil heat flux, γ = psychrometric constant, T = mean air temperature, u2 = wind speed at 2 m, es−ea = vapor pressure deficit, Cn/Cd = reference-crop numerator/denominator constants
entries.description: FAO combination method extended to a cropped surface, accounting for stomatal and soil-surface resistance.

entries.title: Hydrologic Budget (Soil Water)
entries.variables: P = precipitation, Rs = surface runoff, Go = groundwater outflow, Eact = actual evapotranspiration, ΔS = change in soil water storage
entries.description: Water balance of a soil column over a given period.

entries.title: Energy-Budget Method (Evaporation)
entries.formula: Hn = Ha + He + Hg + Hs + Hi
entries.variables: Hn = net radiation, Ha = advected energy, He = latent heat of evaporation, Hg = ground heat flux, Hs = sensible heat, Hi = energy of the water body's initial state
entries.description: Energy balance approach to estimating evaporation from a water body.

entries.title: Lewis-Kostiakov Infiltration Equation
entries.variables: i = cumulative infiltration, f = infiltration rate, c, a = empirical constants, t = time
entries.description: Power-law infiltration model, applicable to soils underlain by impervious layers or for small time values.

entries.title: Horton's Infiltration Equation
entries.variables: fo = initial infiltration rate, fc = final/constant infiltration rate, k = decay constant, t = time
entries.description: Decay-type infiltration model where the rate diminishes toward a constant as the soil profile wets up.

entries.title: Philip's Infiltration Equation
entries.variables: S = sorptivity of the soil, A = soil parameter related to the soil's ability to transmit water, t = time
entries.description: Infiltration model derived from the potential differential equation; accurate for large time values.

entries.title: Green-Ampt Infiltration Equation
entries.formula: fp = K(1 + ηSc/Fp)   or   fp = m + n/Fp
entries.variables: K = hydraulic conductivity, η = porosity, Sc = wetting-front suction head, Fp = cumulative infiltration
entries.description: Physically based infiltration-capacity model derived from Darcy's law.

entries.title: Rational Equation
entries.variables: C = runoff coefficient, i = rainfall intensity, A = drainage area
entries.description: Empirical formula estimating peak runoff rate from a small watershed.

entries.title: Kirpich Formula — Time of Concentration
entries.variables: L = length of the longest flow path, S = watershed slope
entries.description: Required time for a water particle to flow hydraulically from the most distant point in the watershed to the outlet.

entries.title: SCS Lag Formula — Time of Concentration
entries.variables: L = flow length, CN = curve number, S = slope
entries.description: Time of concentration estimated from the lag between the centroid of rainfall excess and the peak of the outflow hydrograph.

entries.title: SCS Curve Number (Runoff) Method
entries.variables: Q = direct runoff, I = rainfall, S = potential maximum retention (mm), CN = curve number
entries.description: Estimates direct storm runoff from rainfall and a land-use/soil based curve number; low CN (sandy/forest) gives low runoff, high CN (clay/paved) gives high runoff.

entries.title: Basic Streamflow Equation
entries.variables: Q = discharge, A = cross-sectional area of flow, V = mean velocity
entries.description: Fundamental discharge equation used for streamflow measurement.

entries.title: Slope-Area (Manning's) Method
entries.variables: k = 1 (metric) or 1.486 (English), n = channel roughness coefficient, R = hydraulic radius, S = channel slope
entries.description: Estimates mean channel velocity from geometry, roughness, and slope for streamflow measurement.

entries.title: Current-Meter Method
entries.variables: a, b = meter calibration constants, N = revolutions of the meter per second
entries.description: Relates a current meter's rotation rate to flow velocity in a stream subsection, for discharge measurement.

entries.title: General Weir Discharge
entries.variables: C = weir coefficient, H = head over the weir crest, n = weir exponent
entries.description: General empirical form used for weirs as indirect flow-measurement structures.

entries.title: Weir Discharge Formulas (Francis, Cipoletti, Triangular)
entries.formula: Francis weir: Q = 1.84LH^(3/2)      Francis w/ contraction: Q = 1.84(L−0.2H)H^(3/2)      Trapezoidal (Cipoletti) weir: Q = 1.86LH^(3/2)      Triangular (90°) weir: Q = 1.38H^(5/2)
entries.variables: L = weir crest length, H = head over the weir
entries.description: Standard discharge formulas for common weir shapes used to measure streamflow.

entries.title: Base Time of a Hydrograph
entries.variables: tp = time to peak, tr = recession time
entries.description: Total duration from the start of rise to the end of the recession limb of a runoff hydrograph.

entries.title: Groundwater (Baseflow) Recession
entries.variables: qt = discharge at time t, q0 = discharge at the starting time, k = recession constant, dt = incremental time
entries.description: Exponential decay of streamflow discharge as it is sustained solely by groundwater drainage.

entries.title: Straight-Line Method (Baseflow Separation)
entries.variables: N = number of days after the peak at which baseflow recession begins, A = drainage area
entries.description: Estimates when direct runoff ends and baseflow recession resumes, for separating a hydrograph.

entries.title: Flood Routing — Storage-Continuity Equation
entries.variables: I = inflow rate, Q = outflow rate, Δt = routing time step
entries.description: Continuity equation underlying hydrologic flood-routing methods: change in storage equals inflow minus outflow volume.

entries.title: Spillway Discharge (used in Modified Pul's Method)
entries.variables: Cd = discharge coefficient, Le = effective crest length, H = head over the spillway/weir
entries.description: Weir-type discharge equation used as the outflow relation in reservoir flood routing.

entries.title: Modified Pul's Method (Storage Routing)
entries.variables: I1, I2 = inflow at start/end of interval, Q1, Q2 = outflow at start/end, S1, S2 = storage at start/end, Δt = time step
entries.description: Reservoir flood-routing method solving the storage-continuity equation for outflow.

entries.title: Goodrich Method (Storage Routing)
entries.variables: I1, I2 = inflow at start/end of interval, Q1, Q2 = outflow at start/end, S1, S2 = storage at start/end, Δt = time step
entries.description: Alternative arrangement of the storage-continuity equation for reservoir flood routing.

entries.title: Total Soil Volume
entries.variables: Va = volume of air, Vw = volume of water, Vs = volume of solid particles
entries.description: Total (bulk) volume of a soil system as the sum of its air, water, and solid fractions.

entries.title: Void Volume
entries.variables: Va = volume of air, Vw = volume of water, VT = total volume, Vs = volume of solids
entries.description: Volume occupied by voids (pore space) in a soil sample.

entries.title: Porosity
entries.variables: Vv = void volume, VT = total volume, BD = bulk density, PD = particle density
entries.description: Ratio of void volume to total soil volume.

entries.title: Volumetric Moisture Content
entries.variables: Vw = volume of water, VT = total volume, MCw = gravimetric (dry-weight) moisture content, As = apparent specific gravity
entries.description: Ratio of the volume of water to the total soil volume.

entries.title: Bulk Density
entries.variables: Ws = dry weight of soil, VT = total soil volume, ρP = particle density, n = porosity
entries.description: Ratio of the dry weight of soil to the total (bulk) soil volume.

entries.title: Particle Density
entries.variables: Ws = dry weight of soil, Vs = volume of solid particles
entries.description: Ratio of the dry weight of soil to the volume of the solid particles alone (average ≈ 2.65 g/cc).

entries.title: Apparent Specific Gravity
entries.variables: ρB = bulk density, ρw = density of water, Rs = real specific gravity, n = porosity
entries.description: Ratio of the bulk density of soil to the density of water.

entries.title: Real Specific Gravity
entries.variables: ρP = particle density, ρw = density of water, Ws = dry weight of soil, Vs = volume of solids
entries.description: Ratio of the particle density of soil to the density of water.

entries.title: Depth of Water Present in Soil
entries.formula: dw = mcv × D = mcw × As × D
entries.variables: mcv = volumetric moisture content, mcw = gravimetric moisture content, As = apparent specific gravity, D = soil depth considered
entries.description: Equivalent depth of water present in the soil at a given moisture condition.

entries.title: Depth of Water Needed
entries.formula: dwn = (mcvf − mcvi) × D = (mcwf − mcwi) × As × D
entries.variables: mcvi/mcvf = initial/final volumetric moisture content, mcwi/mcwf = initial/final gravimetric moisture content, As = apparent specific gravity, D = soil depth
entries.description: Depth of water required to raise soil moisture from an initial to a target final value.

entries.title: Volume of Irrigation Water
entries.variables: dwn = depth of water needed, A = area to be irrigated
entries.description: Volume of water to apply to raise soil moisture over a given area to the target value.

entries.title: Lewis-Kostiakov Infiltration Equation
entries.variables: F = cumulative infiltration, ft = instantaneous infiltration rate at time t, c, α = constants (0<α<1)
entries.description: Empirical infiltration-rate equation used to characterize a furrow or field's infiltration behavior.

entries.title: Horton's Equation (Irrigation Infiltration)
entries.variables: ft = infiltration rate at time t, fc = final constant infiltration rate, fo = initial infiltration capacity, k = decay constant
entries.description: Models the decline of infiltration rate over time during an irrigation event.

entries.title: Philip's Method (Irrigation Infiltration)
entries.variables: F = cumulative infiltration, s = soil sorptivity, A = soil parameter related to transmission ability, t = time
entries.description: Infiltration model relating cumulative and instantaneous infiltration to soil sorptivity.

entries.title: Readily Available Moisture (RAM)
entries.variables: FC = field capacity, PWP = permanent wilting point, As = apparent specific gravity, Drz = root zone depth
entries.description: Portion (≈75%) of available soil moisture that is most easily extracted by plant roots.

entries.title: Moisture Content from % AM Used
entries.variables: FC = field capacity, PWP = permanent wilting point, %AM used = percent of available moisture depleted
entries.description: Computes current soil moisture content given the percent of available moisture already used.

entries.title: Moisture Content from % AM Retained
entries.variables: FC = field capacity, PWP = permanent wilting point, %AM retained = percent of available moisture remaining
entries.description: Computes current soil moisture content given the percent of available moisture still retained.

entries.title: Water Distribution Efficiency
entries.variables: d = average depth of water infiltrated, y = average deviation from d, h1, h2 = depths of penetration measured along the run
entries.description: Uniformity of water applied along a field, expressed relative to the average depth infiltrated.

entries.title: Discharge–Time–Area–Depth Relation
entries.variables: Q = discharge, t = time, A = area irrigated, D = depth applied
entries.description: Basic relation between discharge applied over time and the resulting area-depth of irrigation.

entries.title: Water Conveyance Efficiency
entries.formula: Effc = water delivered / water from source
entries.variables: Water delivered = water reaching the farm, water from source = water diverted from the river/reservoir
entries.description: Ratio between water delivered to the farm and water diverted from the source, expressed in percent.

entries.title: Water Application Efficiency
entries.variables: Water stored = water retained in the farm's root zone, water delivered = water delivered to the farm
entries.description: Ratio of water stored in the root zone during irrigation to the water delivered to the farm.

entries.title: Water Storage Efficiency
entries.formula: Effw = water stored / water needed        Water needed = WHC − (WHC × MAD)
entries.variables: WHC = water-holding capacity, MAD = management allowed deficit
entries.description: Ratio of water stored in the root zone during irrigation to the water needed in the root zone prior to irrigation.

entries.title: Irrigation Water Requirement (IWR)
entries.variables: CWR = crop water requirement, ER = effective rainfall
entries.description: Amount of water to apply as irrigation after deducting effective rainfall from total crop water requirement.

entries.title: Farm Water Requirement (FWR)
entries.formula: FWR = IWR / Application efficiency = IWR + Farm losses
entries.variables: IWR = irrigation water requirement, Application efficiency = efficiency of water use within the farm
entries.description: Total water needed to raise a crop for its entire growth period, including farm-level losses.

entries.title: Farm Application Efficiency (ea)
entries.variables: Qin = water entering the tertiary canal, Qout = water entering the field, S = seepage losses, P = percolation losses, E = evaporation losses
entries.description: Efficiency of water application at the farm/tertiary-canal level.

entries.title: Diversion Water Requirement (DWR)
entries.formula: DWR = FWR / Effc = FWR + conveyance losses
entries.variables: FWR = farm water requirement, Effc = conveyance efficiency
entries.description: Total water diverted from the source needed to meet the farm water requirement, including conveyance losses.

entries.title: Conveyance Efficiency (ec)
entries.variables: Qin = water entering the main canal, Qout = water reaching the tertiary canal, S = seepage, P = percolation, E = evaporation losses
entries.description: Efficiency of water conveyance from the main canal headworks to the tertiary canal.

entries.title: Service Area of an Irrigation System
entries.variables: Dependable Flow = stream's reliable discharge (m³/s), DWR = diversion water requirement (m³/s per ha)
entries.description: Extent of the total service area a national irrigation system's stream can support.

entries.title: Canal Capacity
entries.variables: Q = canal design discharge, area = command area served, water requirement = unit water requirement per hectare
entries.description: Flow a canal must deliver per unit time to serve its command area.

entries.title: Leaching Requirement (LR)
entries.variables: Ddw = depth of drainage water, Diw/Drw = depth of irrigation/rain water, EC(iw+rw) = weighted EC of applied water, ECdw = EC of drainage water
entries.description: Fraction of applied irrigation water that must be leached through the root zone to control soil salinity.

entries.title: Weighted Electrical Conductivity of Applied Water
entries.variables: Diw, Drw = depth of irrigation and rain water, ECiw, ECrw = electrical conductivity of irrigation and rain water
entries.description: Combined salinity of irrigation and rainwater applied to the root zone, used in the leaching requirement equation.

entries.title: Sprinkler Throw
entries.variables: L = lateral spacing, W = wetted diameter, %overlap = design percent overlap between sprinklers
entries.description: Estimates the effective throw distance of a sprinkler given lateral spacing and desired overlap.

entries.title: Emitter Discharge–Pressure Relationship
entries.variables: Q = emitter discharge (L/h), Kd = discharge coefficient characterizing the emitter, H = emitter operating pressure head (m), x = emitter discharge exponent (0 for fully-compensating, up to 0.8 for long-path)
entries.description: Relates a drip/trickle emitter's discharge to its operating pressure head.

entries.title: Land Soaking Requirement (LSR)
entries.formula: LSR = [n − (RMC×As)] × Drz        LSRnet = LSR/ΔT        LSRgross = LSRnet + ET + P
entries.variables: n = soil porosity, RMC = residual moisture content, As = apparent specific gravity, Drz = root zone depth, ΔT = irrigation period, ET = evapotranspiration, P = percolation
entries.description: Water needed to bring a paddy field's soil to saturation prior to transplanting/land preparation.

entries.title: Land Preparation Water Requirement (LPWR)
entries.variables: LSR = land soaking requirement, SW = standing water requirement, ETo = reference evapotranspiration
entries.description: Total water needed to prepare a field for planting, including soaking, standing water, and evapotranspiration.

entries.title: Farm Irrigation Requirement (FIR)
entries.variables: CU = consumptive use, ER = effective rainfall, FL = farm losses (fraction)
entries.description: Net irrigation water needed at the farm, adjusted for on-farm losses.

entries.title: Diversion Water Requirement (Area Basis)
entries.variables: FIR = farm irrigation requirement, A = area, CL = conveyance losses (fraction)
entries.description: Total water to be diverted from the source to meet the farm irrigation requirement over an area, accounting for conveyance losses.

entries.title: Net Application Depth
entries.variables: FC = field capacity, PWP = permanent wilting point, MAD = management allowed deficit, Drz = root zone depth, RAM = readily available moisture, WHC = water holding capacity, MCv = volumetric moisture content
entries.description: Net depth of water to be applied per irrigation to refill the root zone.

entries.title: Drain Spacing — Steady State, Unconfined Aquifer, With Recharge, Equal Drain Elevation
entries.variables: L = drain spacing, k = soil hydraulic conductivity, H = depth of water midway between drains, D = depth of water inside the drains, R = net recharge into the drained area
entries.description: Drain spacing for a drain bottom reaching the impermeable layer, unconfined aquifer, uniform recharge, equal drain elevations.

entries.title: Drain Spacing — Steady State, Unconfined Aquifer, No Recharge, Unequal Drain Elevation
entries.variables: L = drain spacing, k = hydraulic conductivity, h1, h2 = water depths at the drains, q = flow into the drain per unit width
entries.description: Drain spacing for unidirectional flow to the lower drain, no recharge, unconfined aquifer.

entries.title: Drain Spacing — Steady State, Confined Aquifer, No Recharge, Unequal Drain Elevation
entries.variables: L = drain spacing, b = thickness of the confined aquifer (strip to be drained), k = hydraulic conductivity, h1, h2 = water depths at the drains, q = flow into the drain per unit width
entries.description: Drain spacing for unidirectional flow to the lower drain, no recharge, confined aquifer.

entries.title: Flow Into the Drain — With Recharge, Equal Elevation (Left/Right Drain)
entries.formula: Flow to left drain: qL = −RL/2 − k(h2²−h1²)/(2L)        Flow to right drain: qR = −RL/2 − k(h2²−h1²)/(2L)
entries.variables: R = net recharge, L = drain spacing, k = hydraulic conductivity, h1, h2 = water depths at the drains
entries.description: Discharge into each of two drains of equal elevation under uniform recharge, unconfined aquifer (as printed in source for both directions).

entries.title: Water Table Elevation at a Point x Between Drains
entries.variables: R = net recharge, k = hydraulic conductivity, L = drain spacing, x = distance from the left drain, h1, h2 = water depths at the drains
entries.description: Height of the water table at any point x between two drains under recharge.

entries.title: Stagnation Point Between Drains
entries.variables: L = drain spacing, k = hydraulic conductivity, h1, h2 = water depths at the drains, R = net recharge
entries.description: Location between two drains where groundwater flow divides toward each drain.

entries.title: Maximum Water Table Elevation Between Drains
entries.variables: R = net recharge, k = hydraulic conductivity, L = drain spacing, xs = stagnation point, h1, h2 = water depths at the drains
entries.description: Highest elevation the water table reaches between two drains, occurring at the stagnation point.

entries.title: Hooghoudt's Equation (Drain Bottom Not Reaching Impermeable Layer)
entries.variables: k1 = hydraulic conductivity of the soil above drain level, k2 = hydraulic conductivity of the soil below drain level, d = equivalent depth to the impermeable layer, h = height of water table above drain level, q = drainage rate
entries.description: Steady-state drain spacing equation for drains that do not reach the impermeable layer.

entries.title: Glover-Dumm Formula (Unsteady-State Drain Spacing)
entries.variables: k = hydraulic conductivity, d = effective depth to the impermeable layer, μ = drainable pore space, ho = initial height of water table midway between drains, ht = height of water table midway between drains at time t, t = time to drain
entries.description: Drain spacing equation for the falling water-table (unsteady-state) condition after a recharge event.

entries.title: Gross Depth of Application
entries.variables: dnet = net application depth, Ea = application efficiency
entries.description: Total depth of water to apply, including losses, to deliver the net depth needed by the crop.

entries.title: Irrigation Interval
entries.variables: dnet = net application depth, CU = consumptive use, ETcrop = crop evapotranspiration, FC = field capacity, PWP = permanent wilting point, MAD = management allowed deficit, Drz = root zone depth, RAM = readily available moisture, WHC = water holding capacity
entries.description: Time between successive irrigations, based on how fast the crop depletes the net application depth.

entries.title: Irrigation Period
entries.variables: A = area to be irrigated, dgross = gross application depth, Q = discharge/flow rate applied
entries.description: Time required to apply the gross depth of water to an area at a given discharge.

entries.title: Irrigation Efficiency
entries.variables: CU = consumptive use, ER = effective rainfall, Wf = water furnished/applied (CU, ER, Wf in m³)
entries.description: Overall efficiency of an irrigation system, comparing net crop water need to total water furnished.

entries.title: Froude Number (Open Channel Flow)
entries.variables: V = flow velocity, D = hydraulic depth (flow area / top width), g = gravitational acceleration
entries.description: Dimensionless ratio of inertial to gravitational forces used to classify open-channel flow: F<1 subcritical, F=1 critical, F>1 supercritical.

entries.title: Critical Flow Velocity (Open Channel)
entries.variables: V = critical velocity, g = gravitational acceleration, D = hydraulic depth
entries.description: Flow velocity at critical state (Froude number = 1) in an open channel.

entries.title: Trapezoidal/Rectangular/Triangular Channel Geometry
entries.formula: Trapezoidal: A = by+zy², P = b+2y√(1+z²), T = b+2zy      Rectangular (z=0): A = by, P = b+2y, T = b      Triangular (b=0): A = zy², P = 2y√(1+z²), T = 2zy      R = A/P, D = A/T
entries.variables: b = bottom width, y = depth of flow, z = side slope, A = flow area, P = wetted perimeter, T = top width, R = hydraulic radius, D = hydraulic depth
entries.description: Standard open-channel section geometry; rectangular and triangular sections are special cases of the trapezoidal formula.

entries.title: Best Hydraulic Cross-Section (Canal Side Slope)
entries.formula: Concrete canals: b = 2ytan(θ/2)   t = b+2y/tanθ      Unlined canals: b = 4ytan(θ/2)   T = b+2y/tanθ
entries.variables: b = bottom width, y = depth of flow, θ = side-slope angle, t/T = top width
entries.description: Optimum bottom-width-to-depth relations for the most hydraulically efficient canal cross-section.

entries.title: Specific Energy (Open Channel)
entries.variables: y = depth of flow, V = velocity, Q = discharge, A = flow area, g = gravitational acceleration
entries.description: Sum of the depth of flow and the velocity head at a channel cross-section.

entries.title: Critical Flow Condition (Open Channel)
entries.variables: A = flow area, T = top width, Q = discharge, g = gravitational acceleration
entries.description: Relates channel area and top width to discharge and gravity at critical depth (Froude number = 1).

entries.title: Orifice Flow (Open Channel Measurement)
entries.variables: h = depth of water above the opening, g = gravitational acceleration, Cd = discharge coefficient, A = orifice area
entries.description: Velocity and discharge through a sharp-edged orifice used as an open-channel flow-measuring device.

entries.title: Piston Displacement
entries.variables: D = cylinder bore, L = stroke length
entries.description: Volume displaced by the piston as it travels the length of one stroke.

entries.title: Compression Ratio
entries.variables: PD = piston displacement, CV = clearance volume
entries.description: Ratio of total cylinder volume (at BDC) to clearance volume (at TDC).

entries.title: Camshaft Speed
entries.variables: Applies to a 4-stroke engine, where the camshaft turns at half crankshaft speed
entries.description: Relates camshaft rotational speed to crankshaft speed in a 4-stroke engine.

entries.title: Number of Explosions per Cylinder (4-Stroke)
entries.formula: Number of explosions = (Crankshaft revolutions)/2 = Camshaft revolutions
entries.variables: Applies per cylinder, per unit time
entries.description: Number of power (combustion) events per cylinder relative to crankshaft and camshaft revolutions in a 4-stroke engine.

entries.title: Crankshaft–Camshaft Speed Relation (2-Stroke)
entries.variables: Applies to a 2-stroke engine, unlike the 4-stroke 2:1 ratio
entries.description: In a 2-stroke engine the camshaft (or equivalent timing element) turns at the same speed as the crankshaft.

entries.title: Explosions per Minute (Multi-Cylinder Engine)
entries.formula: Explosions per minute = Camshaft RPM × No. of cylinders
entries.variables: Camshaft RPM = camshaft rotational speed, No. of cylinders = number of engine cylinders
entries.description: Total number of combustion events per minute across all cylinders of an engine.

entries.title: Firing Interval
entries.formula: Firing Interval = (360° × No. of strokes) / No. of cylinders
entries.variables: No. of strokes = strokes per cycle (2 or 4), No. of cylinders = number of cylinders
entries.description: Crank angle between successive firing (power) events in a multi-cylinder engine.

entries.title: Total Engine Displacement
entries.formula: Total Displacement = (Area of Piston × Stroke Length) × No. of Cylinders
entries.variables: Area of Piston = piston cross-sectional area, Stroke Length = piston travel per stroke
entries.description: Total swept volume of all cylinders in an engine.

entries.title: Engine Torque
entries.formula: Torque = Force × Moment Arm, where Force = Area of Piston × Pressure, Moment Arm = ½ × bore
entries.variables: Force = force on the piston, Pressure = combustion pressure, bore = cylinder bore diameter
entries.description: Torque produced at the crankshaft from combustion pressure acting on the piston.

entries.title: Engine Power
entries.variables: F = force, L = length of arm (torque arm), N = rpm, T = torque
entries.description: Mechanical power output of an engine from force/torque and rotational speed.

entries.title: Brake Horsepower (BHP)
entries.variables: T = torque, N = rpm
entries.description: Power measured at the engine's output shaft (drive shaft or crankshaft).

entries.title: Indicated Horsepower (IHP)
entries.variables: P = mean effective pressure, L = stroke length, A = piston area, N = engine speed, n = number of cylinders, c = a constant for units, FHP = friction horsepower
entries.description: Power generated inside the combustion chamber, before mechanical losses are subtracted.

entries.title: Mechanical Efficiency
entries.variables: BHP = brake horsepower, IHP = indicated horsepower
entries.description: Fraction of indicated power that is actually delivered at the output shaft.

entries.title: Fuel Consumption
entries.formula: Fuel Consumption (lph) = ΔFuel volume / # of hours of operation
entries.variables: ΔFuel volume = volume of fuel consumed, # of hours of operation = time operated
entries.description: Rate of fuel use by an engine, in liters per hour.

entries.title: Specific Fuel Consumption
entries.formula: Specific fuel consumption (l/hp-hr) = fuel consumption / power
entries.variables: fuel consumption = rate of fuel use, power = engine power output
entries.description: Fuel used per unit of power output per hour, a measure of engine fuel economy.

entries.title: Indicated Thermal Efficiency
entries.variables: IHP = indicated horsepower, fuel energy = energy supplied by the fuel burned
entries.description: Fraction of the fuel's energy converted into indicated power.

entries.title: Brake Thermal Efficiency
entries.variables: BHP = brake horsepower, fuel energy = energy supplied by the fuel burned
entries.description: Fraction of the fuel's energy converted into usable brake power.

entries.title: Fuel Energy (Engine Test)
entries.formula: Fuel Energy (hp) = Heating Value × Fuel Consumption
entries.variables: Heating Value = calorific value of the fuel, Fuel Consumption = rate of fuel use
entries.description: Rate of energy supplied to the engine by the fuel being burned, used as the denominator in thermal efficiency calculations.

entries.title: Octane Rating
entries.formula: Octane Rating = Volume of Isooctane / Total Volume
entries.variables: Volume of Isooctane = isooctane content in the reference blend, Total Volume = total fuel blend volume
entries.description: Measure of a gasoline's resistance to knocking, based on an isooctane/heptane reference blend.

entries.title: Cetane Rating
entries.variables: %N-cetane = percent normal cetane, %HMN = percent heptamethylnonane
entries.description: Measure of a diesel fuel's ignition quality (how readily it self-ignites under compression).

entries.title: Fuel Thermal Efficiency
entries.formula: TE = Useful energy output / Energy provided by fuel
entries.variables: Useful energy output = usable work/energy delivered, Energy provided by fuel = total energy content of fuel consumed
entries.description: Fraction of a fuel's energy content converted into useful output.

entries.title: Energy Provided by Fuel
entries.formula: Energy provided by fuel (MJ) = fuel (kg) × energy content (MJ/kg)
entries.variables: fuel = mass of fuel consumed, energy content = calorific/heat value of the fuel per unit mass
entries.description: Total energy available from a given mass of fuel, based on its heat value.

entries.title: Rolling Resistance Force
entries.variables: m = mass, g = gravitational acceleration, coeff = rolling resistance coefficient
entries.description: Force resisting a tractor/implement's motion due to rolling resistance, used to compute drawbar power.

entries.title: Drawbar Power (DBP)
entries.variables: F = rolling resistance (or pulling) force, Speed = travel speed
entries.description: Power available at a tractor's drawbar to pull loads such as plows, harrows, or trailers.

entries.title: Human Power Output
entries.variables: P = power output (hp), t = time in minutes
entries.description: Estimates sustainable human power output as a function of the duration of work.

entries.title: Manure (Dung) Weight Produced
entries.formula: Weight of dung = manure available × no. of animals × days
entries.variables: manure available = daily manure production rate per animal (kg/day-animal), no. of animals = animal count, days = retention/collection period
entries.description: Total manure weight produced by a group of animals over a given period, used in farm power/biogas planning.

entries.title: Draft Load (Multiple Draft Animals)
entries.variables: Draft = single-animal draft capacity, factor = harnessing factor for the number of animals hitched together
entries.description: Adjusts the usable draft (pulling) load when multiple draft animals are harnessed together, accounting for reduced efficiency per additional animal.
